function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Use for system operations, file management, running scripts, curl, and any command-line tasks. Prefer this over code_run(python) for simple shell operations like curl, ls, cat, grep, etc.

function.name: code_run
function.description: Code executor. Prefer python. No concurrent calls. Prefer code in reply body to avoid escaping. No hardcoding bulk data

script.description: [Mutually exclusive] NEVER use this param when use reply code block.

function.name: read
function.description: Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool. By default, it reads up to 500 lines starting from the beginning of the file. You can optionally specify a line offset and limit (especially handy for long files). Results are returned with line numbers starting at 1. A negative offset anchors at the end of the file and reads the last min(|offset|, limit) lines (e.g. offset=-50 reads the last 50 lines; offset=-50 with limit=10 reads the last 10 lines). Pages are capped by a character budget, so a page may contain fewer lines than requested. Lines are kept whole whenever possible; only a single line exceeding the page budget is cut mid-line and marked [TRUNCATED] (a tail page keeps the end of that line). If output ends with a truncation marker, continue with the indicated offset/limit to read the remaining older lines.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from (1-based). A negative value anchors at the end of the file: it reads the last min(|offset|, limit) lines (e.g. offset=-50 = last 50 lines; with limit=10 = last 10 lines). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

limit.description: The number of lines to read. With a negative offset it shrinks the tail window from the older end (offset=-50 limit=10 = last 10 lines). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once. Maximum 500.

function.name: write
function.description: Writes a file to the local filesystem. This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path. Use mode='append' to append content to the end of the file.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write to

content.description: The content to write to the file

mode.description: Write mode: 'overwrite' replaces the entire file, 'append' adds content to the end. Default: overwrite.

function.name: edit
function.description: Performs exact string replacements in files. The edit will FAIL if old_string is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use replace_all to change every instance of old_string.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The text to replace (must be different from new_string)

new_string.description: The text to replace it with

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

function.name: grep
function.description: Search for a pattern in files. Returns matching lines with line numbers. Supports regular expressions. Useful for finding where a symbol is defined, where a function is called, or searching for any text pattern across files.

pattern.description: The pattern to search for (supports regular expressions)

path.description: The directory or file to search in (absolute path). Defaults to current working directory.

include.description: File pattern to include (e.g. '*.py', '*.ts'). If not provided, searches all files.
